The last race of the evening was the One Mile event, but whereas the Croydon Club had saved two of their outstanding performers in Hancock, who has come to the front with such rapidity, and Chilton, a former Surrey County champion; we knew that we could not hope to fare as well in this race as in the others.

The two men referred to (Burt and Hancock) scored between them 36 of our rivals' 117 points. Burt used to be a prominent distance runner in the Blackheath Harriers ranks; while Hancock was running over the country less than a year ago, but now appears to be a Walking Champion in embryo.
In the last event of the evening, the 1 mile, honours went to Hancock and Bell, of Surrey W.C., who took the first two places, with Denyer, of the Poly, third.

Here we had Don Brown, fresh from his win in the Surrey County Championship, and Percy Wright, opposed by Hancock and Amer, of S.W.C. Our chance had gone, but our rivalry still continued, and there was still second place in the competition to be consolidated.
